correctness.rationale: The whole-disk holomorphic space has basis z^n for n>=0, monomial norms B(n+b,m+1)/B(b,m+1) with b=beta+1>=1, so K is a positive scalar times P_{m,b}(s)/(1-s)^(m+2). Applying Euler derivative to rising factorial generating functions independently reconstructed all five exact resultant polynomials Res_s(P,s^(m+1)P(1/s)); for m<=3 they never vanish at b>=1; for m=4 the only possible boundary value is b=2. All P_{m,1} are constants (m+1)!, hence zero-free up to the crossing. At b=2, independent symbolic factoring obtained -120(s-2)(s^2-3s+3)(s^2-s+1), two simple critical roots e^{±iπ/3}, and implicit differentiation gave d|s|^2/db=-49/360: both enter for b>2. For b>2 no further resultant zeros; nonzero discriminant certifies two simple interior zeros. Counts of scalar zeros correspond to two-variable zero fibres for |s|<1. The restriction to integer boundary m=0..4, origin beta>=0, and whole-disk (NOT punctured Laurent space) is essential; numerical samples are not proof.

value.rationale: A complete zero-free/zeros phase diagram for the first five integer boundary exponents and every positive origin exponent is a natural initial classification in the Lu Qi-Keng problem. First nontrivial m=4 transition, exactly two simple zeros and a quantitative transversal crossing provide a precise nonmechanical structural fact, beyond mere moment formulas or isolated parameter examples.
